description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join a robotics team developing systems for complex maintenance tasks in service environments. You will integrate hardware, build teleoperation capabilities, and run experiments to identify and remove barriers to reliable robot performance.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Diagnose robot capabilities and limitations in service bay conditions, identifying hardware and software bottlenecks.

 - Design and build teleoperation rigs that integrate robot arms, end effectors, cameras, and VR or leader-follower control systems.

 - Break complex repair tasks into testable subtasks and validate robot performance on each.

 - Isolate failure causes across operator visibility, control latency, perception, motion control, reach, and dexterity.

 - Run controlled experiments involving force feedback, force/torque sensing, compliant control, and tooling improvements.

 - Measure completion rates, cycle times, and human interventions, and record synchronized sensor data for learning algorithms.

 - Move validated tasks from bench experiments to supervised trials in real service environments.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging physical robots; the role description does not specify a required number of years.

 - Strong manipulation or teleoperation experience and proficiency in C++, Python, and ROS 2 or equivalent frameworks.

 - Ability to design experiments that distinguish software limitations from hardware constraints.

 - A rigorous approach to safety when robots operate around people and vehicles.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary of $205,000 to $305,000 annually, plus stock options. Visa sponsorship is not available.


LOCATION

On-site in the United States.
